title: Western Chu
capsule: Western Chu was the dominant state of the Chu-Han interregnum (206–202 BCE) under Xiang Yu, who had led the coalition that destroyed the Qin dynasty and distributed the empire into Eighteen Kingdoms at Hongmen in 206 BCE. Xiang Yu styled himself 'Hegemon-King of Western Chu' and ruled the lower Yangtze basin and Huai River valley from Pengcheng (modern Xuzhou). Despite early military superiority, Xiang Yu was outmaneuvered politically by Liu Bang of Han, whose generals韓信 (Han Xin) encircled Western Chu at the Battle of Gaixia in 202 BCE; Xiang Yu refused surrender and died by suicide at the Wu River, ending Western Chu and enabling the founding of the Han dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Western Chu's core territories are broadly reconstructed from Shiji and Hanshu sources; the precise boundaries of its claimed domains are not mapped in contemporaneous cartography.
